source_text: των εὐδοκιμήσεσι, καὶ μιμητὰς ἀναφαίνεσθαι τῆς τῶν πατέρων εὐκλείας, κατ' ἴχνος ἰόντας τῆς ἐκείνων λατρείας, καὶ τὴν φιλαιτάτην τῷ Θεῷ προσκομίζοντας εὐωδίαν, οὐ μεμερισμένως, ἀλλ' ὁλοτελῶς. Τοῦτο γὰρ, οἶμαι, ἐστὶ τὸ, «Πᾶσα θυσία ἱερέως ὁλόκαυτος ἔσται.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἑαυτοὺς οὖν ἄρα προσοίσομεν, καὶ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας ἀνακεισόμεθα τῷ Θεῷ, τὴν τῶν ἁγίων ἰχνηλατοῦντες ζωὴν, καὶ ταῖς ἐκείνων ἱερουργίαις ἑπόμενοι, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι ταῖς πνευματικαῖς. {ΚΥΡ.} Πάνυ μὲν οὖν, ὦ Παλλάδιε. Πλὴν ὅτι τὸ ἀποτρίψασθαι μολυσμὸν, καὶ διαδράναι τὴν ἁμαρτίαν, οὐχ ἑτέρως ἂν γένοιτο καὶ ἐνυπάρξαι τισὶν, ἢ ὅτι διὰ μόνου Χριστοῦ, ἐν ᾧ καὶ δι' οὗ πᾶσα κάθαρσις, τὴν σωτήριον ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ὑπομείναντος σφαγὴν, ἀναμάθοι τις ἂν, καὶ οὐκ εἰς μακρὰν, διά τε τοῦ γείτονος καὶ συνεζευγμένου θεσπίσματος· ἔχει γὰρ ὧδε· «Καὶ ἐλάλησε Κύριος πρὸς Μωσῆν, λέγων· Λάλησον τῷ Ἀαρὼν καὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς αὐτοῦ, λέγων· Οὗτος ὁ νόμος τῆς ἁμαρτίας· ἐν τόπῳ οὗ σφάξουσι τὸ ὁλοκαύτωμα, σφάξουσι τὰ περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἔναντι Κυρίου· Ἅγια ἁγίων ἐστίν. Ὁ ἱερεὺς ἀναφέρων αὐτὴν, ἔδεται αὐτήν· ἐν τόπῳ ἁγίῳ βρωθήσεται, ἐν αὐλῇ τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου. Πᾶς ὁ ἁπτόμενος τῶν κρεῶν αὐτῆς, ἁγιασθήσεται· καὶ ᾧ ἐὰν ἐπιῤῥαντισθῇ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος αὐτῆς ἐπὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον, ὃς ἐὰν ῥαντισθῇ ἐπ' αὐτὸ, πλυθήσεται ἐν τόπῳ ἁγίῳ· καὶ σκεῦος ὀστράκινον οὗ ἐὰν ἑψηθῇ ἐν αὐτῷ, συντριβήσεται· ἐὰν δὲ ἐν σκεύει χαλκῷ ἑψηθῇ, ἐκτρίψει αὐτὸ, καὶ ἐκκλύσει ὕδατι. Πᾶς ἄρσην ἐν τοῖς ἱερεῦσι φάγεται αὐτά· Ἅγια ἁγίων ἐστὶ Κυρίῳ.» Ἱερεῖον μὲν οὖν τὸ περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας εἴη ἂν ἕτερον οὐδὲν παρὰ τὸν Ἐμμανουὴλ, ὅς ἐστιν ἀμνὸς ὁ ἀληθινὸς ὁ αἴρων τὰς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ κόσμου. Σφάζεται δὲ ἐν τόπῳ τοῦ ὁλοκαυτώματος· οὐ γάρ τοι μερικῶς τε καὶ καθ' ἡμᾶς ἅγιος ὁ Χριστὸς (οὐ γὰρ ἐποίησεν ἁμαρτίαν), εὐώδης δὲ ὅλος καὶ ἱερὸς, καὶ ἁγιασμοῦ τοῖς ἄλλοις ἅπασι χορηγός. Εἰ γὰρ καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἀνόμοις ἐλογίσθη καὶ τοῖς κατακεκριμένοις ἐναρίθμιος γέγονεν οἰκονομικῶς· ἀλλ' οἶδεν ἅγιον ὄντα καὶ ἱερὸν τὸν τοῦ Υἱοῦ θάνατον ὁ Πατήρ. Ταύτῃτοί φησιν· «Ἐν τόπῳ οὗ σφάξουσι τὸ ὁλοκαύτωμα, σφάξουσι καὶ τὸ περὶ ἁμαρτίας· Ἅγια ἁγίων ἐστίν.» Ὥσπερ γὰρ Θεὸς θεῶν ἐστιν ὁ Υἱὸς, οὕτω καὶ ἁγίων Ἅγιος, ὅλην αὐτὸς ἁγιάζων τὴν κτίσιν τῷ ἰδίῳ πνεύματι, καθὸ πέφυκεν ἐκ Πατρὸς, καὶ ἔστι Θεὸς ἀληθῶς. Ἔδεται δὲ τὴν θυσίαν, φησὶν, ὁ προσκομίζων αὐτὴν ἱερεύς. Ἕκαστος γὰρ, οἶμαι, τῶν εἰς λειτουργίαν τὴν ἱερὰν ἠγμένων, τοὺς καρποὺς τῶν ἰδίων ἀποτρυγήσει πόνων, καὶ τῆς ἑαυτοῦ λειτουργίας ἐκθεριεῖ τὴν ἀντίδοσιν. Ἐσθίεται δὲ τῆς θυσίας τὸ λείψανον ἐν ἁγίοις τόποις, καὶ ἐν αὐλῇ τῆς ἁγίας σκηνῆς. Προσάγεται γὰρ ἐν ἐκκλησίαις τὰ μυστικὰ, καὶ τῆς ἁγίας τραπέζης Χριστοῦ τὸ ἀπόλεκτον ἐν αὐταῖς ἀξιοῦται γένος. Ἔνθα δ' ἂν ἱερατεύει νόμιμος ἱερεὺς, ἅγιος ἔσται τόπος. Ἁγιάζει δὲ τὸν ἁπτόμενον ἡ θυσία, καὶ ὁ τοῦ αἵματος ῥαντισμός. Προσ
pass_a_gloss: [follow the] good repute [of those who went before], and appear imitators of the glory of the fathers, going in the track of their worship, and bringing to God the fragrance dearest to him, not divided, but wholly. For this, I think, is the saying: 'Every sacrifice of a priest shall be wholly burnt.' PALL.: So then we shall offer ourselves, and be dedicated to God for an odour of fragrance, tracking the life of the saints, and following their sacred rites, clearly the spiritual ones. CYR.: Very much so, Palladius. Except that to wipe off defilement and to escape sin could not come about or be present in anyone otherwise than through Christ alone, in whom and through whom is all cleansing, who endured the saving slaughter for us: one could learn this, and not at length, through the neighbouring and joined oracle; for it runs thus: 'And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the sin offering; in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering they shall slaughter the things for sin before the Lord; it is holy of holies. The priest who offers it shall eat it; in a holy place it shall be eaten, in the court of the tent of witness. Everyone touching its flesh shall be sanctified; and on whatever garment some of its blood is sprinkled, whatever it is sprinkled on shall be washed in a holy place; and an earthen vessel in which it is boiled shall be broken; but if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, he shall scour it and rinse it with water. Every male among the priests shall eat them; it is holy of holies to the Lord.' The victim for sin then would be nothing other than Emmanuel, who is the true lamb who takes away the sins of the world. And he is slaughtered in the place of the whole burnt offering; for Christ is not partly holy and as we are (for he did no sin), but wholly fragrant and sacred, and supplier of holiness to all the others. For even if he was reckoned among the lawless and became numbered with the condemned by the economy, yet the Father knows the death of the Son as being holy and sacred. Therefore he says: 'In the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering they shall slaughter also the sin offering; it is holy of holies.' For as the Son is God of gods, so also Holy of holies, himself sanctifying the whole creation by his own spirit, inasmuch as he is by nature from the Father and is truly God. And the priest who brings the sacrifice, he says, shall eat it. For each one, I think, of those brought into the sacred ministry will gather the fruits of his own labours and harvest the return of his own ministry. And the remnant of the sacrifice is eaten in holy places and in the court of the holy tent. For the mysteries are brought forward in churches, and the chosen race is counted worthy of the holy table of Christ in them. And wherever a lawful priest serves as priest, it will be a holy place. And the sacrifice sanctifies the one touching, and the sprinkling of the blood. For we [draw near]
pass_b_english: Cyril: …the good record of those who went before them, and show themselves imitators of the fathers' glory, following in the footsteps of their worship and bringing to God the fragrance dearest to him, not in part but wholly. For this, I think, is what is meant by ‘Every sacrifice of a priest shall be wholly burnt’ (Leviticus 6:23).
Palladius: Then we shall offer ourselves and be dedicated to God as a fragrant aroma, following in the footsteps of the saints’ life and keeping to their sacred rites, the spiritual ones, plainly.

Cyril: Certainly, Palladius. But to wipe away defilement and escape from sin could not come about or be found in anyone in any other way than through Christ alone, in whom and through whom is all cleansing, who endured the saving slaughter for us. One may learn this without going far, from the decree that stands next to it and is joined to it. It runs thus: ‘And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying: This is the law of the sin offering. In the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering, they shall slaughter the sin offerings before the Lord; they are most holy. The priest who offers it shall eat it; it shall be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the tent of witness. Everyone who touches its flesh shall be made holy; and if any of its blood is sprinkled on a garment, whatever it is sprinkled on shall be washed in a holy place. And an earthen vessel in which it is boiled shall be broken; but if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, he shall scour it and rinse it with water. Every male among the priests shall eat them; they are most holy to the Lord’ (Leviticus 6:24–29).

The victim for sin, then, could be none other than Emmanuel, who is the true Lamb who takes away the sins of the world (John 1:29). And he is slaughtered in the place of the whole burnt offering. For Christ is not holy in part, as we are, for he committed no sin (1 Peter 2:22); he is wholly fragrant and sacred, and the giver of holiness to all others. For even if he was reckoned among the lawless (Isaiah 53:12) and, in the divine plan, was counted among the condemned, the Father knows the death of the Son to be holy and sacred. That is why he says: ‘In the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering, they shall slaughter the sin offering also; it is most holy’ (Leviticus 6:25). For just as the Son is God of gods, so also is he Holy of holies, himself making the whole creation holy by his own Spirit, since he is by nature from the Father and is truly God.

The priest who brings the sacrifice, he says, shall eat it. For each one, I think, who has been brought into the sacred ministry will gather the fruit of his own labors and reap the reward of his own service. And what remains of the sacrifice is eaten in holy places and in the court of the holy tent (Leviticus 6:26). For the mysteries are offered in churches, and in them the chosen race is counted worthy of the holy table of Christ. And wherever a lawful priest serves, the place will be holy. And the sacrifice makes holy the one who touches it, and so does the sprinkling of the blood (Leviticus 6:27). For we draw near…

choices.english: the good record of those who went before them
choices.why: Opens mid-sentence: the clause began at the end of §24 ('one must follow the [good record] of those who went before'); the fragment 'των εὐδοκιμήσεσι' is rendered 'the good record of those who went before them'.
In 6:23 LXX θυσία renders the Hebrew grain offering; kept as 'sacrifice' because Cyril reads it of the priest's self-offering.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 12 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-sentence: the clause began at the end of §24 ('one must follow the [good record] of those who went before'); the fragment 'των εὐδοκιμήσεσι' is rendered 'the good record of those who went before them'. Ends mid-word on 'Προσ', completed as 'Προσίεμεν' at the head of §26, so the English breaks at 'For we draw near…'. Leviticus references use English numbering; Rahlfs LXX numbers these verses 6:16 (=Eng. 6:23) and 6:17-22 (=Eng. 6:24-29). In 6:23 LXX θυσία renders the Hebrew grain offering; kept as 'sacrifice' because Cyril reads it of the priest's self-offering. 'οὐ γὰρ ἐποίησεν ἁμαρτίαν' matches 1 Peter 2:22 (cf. Isaiah 53:9); 'ἐν τοῖς ἀνόμοις ἐλογίσθη' is Isaiah 53:12 (quoted in Luke 22:37). 'Θεὸς θεῶν' is a scriptural title (Deuteronomy 10:17; Psalm 50:1 [LXX 49:1]; Psalm 136:2 [LXX 135:2]) but no single source is clear, so it is uncited. 'τὸ ἀπόλεκτον γένος' may echo 1 Peter 2:9 (γένος ἐκλεκτόν) but the wording differs; uncited. 'τῷ ἰδίῳ πνεύματι' taken as the Holy Spirit, proper to the Son (Cyril's usage), hence 'his own Spirit'. The earlier listing of 2 Corinthians 5:21 and Hebrews 13:10 for this section is not supported by the Greek and is dropped.

Drafted Pass A, kept as written (rewritten as a literal English gloss from the Greek in pass_a_gloss): [continuing from §24: one must follow] the εὐδοκιμήσεις (approved deeds, good record) of those who went before, and appear μιμηταί (imitators) of the fathers' εὔκλεια (glory), going κατ' ἴχνος (in the track) of their λατρεία (worship), and bringing to God the εὐωδία (fragrance) dearest to him, οὐ μεμερισμένως ἀλλ' ὁλοτελῶς (not divided/in part, but wholly). This, I think, is 'Every θυσία of a priest shall be ὁλόκαυτος (wholly burnt)'. PALL.: So we shall προσοίσομεν (offer) ourselves and ἀνακεισόμεθα (be dedicated) to God εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, ἰχνηλατοῦντες (tracking) the ζωή of the ἅγιοι and following their ἱερουργίαι (sacred rites), plainly the πνευματικαί. CYR.: Quite so, Palladius. Except that ἀποτρίψασθαι μολυσμόν (to wipe off defilement) and διαδράναι τὴν ἁμαρτίαν (escape sin) could not happen or be present in anyone otherwise than through Christ alone, in whom and through whom is all κάθαρσις, who ὑπομείναντος (endured) τὴν σωτήριον σφαγήν (saving slaughter) for us; one may learn it not far off from the γείτων καὶ συνεζευγμένον θέσπισμα (neighboring, joined decree). Quote Lev 6:24-29 (LXX 6:17-22): law of the ἁμαρτία (sin offering); slaughtered where the ὁλοκαύτωμα is slaughtered, ἔναντι Κυρίου; ἅγια ἁγίων; the priest ἀναφέρων eats it in a holy place, in the αὐλή of the σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου; whoever touches its κρέα ἁγιασθήσεται; garment sprinkled with blood washed in a holy place; σκεῦος ὀστράκινον in which it is boiled συντριβήσεται; if bronze, ἐκτρίψει and ἐκκλύσει ὕδατι; every ἄρσην among the priests eats; ἅγια ἁγίων Κυρίῳ. The ἱερεῖον for sin is none other than Ἐμμανουήλ, the ἀμνὸς ὁ ἀληθινός who αἴρων τὰς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ κόσμου. Slaughtered in the place of the ὁλοκαύτωμα: Christ not holy μερικῶς καὶ καθ' ἡμᾶς (partially, as we are), for οὐκ ἐποίησεν ἁμαρτίαν; but εὐώδης ὅλος καὶ ἱερός and ἁγιασμοῦ χορηγός (supplier of sanctification) to all others. Though ἐν τοῖς ἀνόμοις ἐλογίσθη and was counted among the κατακεκριμένοι οἰκονομικῶς (by the economy), the Father knows the Son's θάνατος to be ἅγιος and ἱερός. Hence: in the place of the whole burnt offering they shall slaughter the sin offering; ἅγια ἁγίων. As the Son is Θεὸς θεῶν, so ἁγίων Ἅγιος, himself ἁγιάζων all κτίσις τῷ ἰδίῳ πνεύματι, καθὸ πέφυκεν ἐκ Πατρός (as by nature from the Father) and is Θεὸς ἀληθῶς. The προσκομίζων priest eats the θυσία: each one ἠγμένος into the ἱερὰ λειτουργία ἀποτρυγήσει (will gather the vintage of) his own πόνοι and ἐκθεριεῖ (reap) the ἀντίδοσις (repayment) of his λειτουργία. The λείψανον (remainder) is eaten in holy places and in the court of the holy tent: τὰ μυστικά are offered ἐν ἐκκλησίαις, and in them τὸ ἀπόλεκτον γένος (the chosen race) ἀξιοῦται of the holy τράπεζα of Christ. Where a νόμιμος ἱερεύς ἱερατεύει, the τόπος will be ἅγιος. The θυσία ἁγιάζει the one touching, and the ῥαντισμός of the blood. Προσ[ίεμεν, continued in §26]…
